# synology_share_permissions (Resource)

Own the complete explicit local-user and local-group permission policy for one shared folder. Each map value is read_only, read_write or deny. Omission means no explicit grant or deny, rather than denial. Effective access also depends on group membership and file ACLs. Import by shared-folder name to preserve an existing policy. Creating this configuration resource applies the declared policy. Destroy only releases management and leaves permissions unchanged. When managing accounts in the same configuration, depend on all account resources so policy snapshots run after account creation.

## Adopt existing settings

Use an initialized project from [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Add this import block with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_share_permissions.archive
  id = "archive"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with the values DSM currently reports. Use the sample configuration as a starting point.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. For one import, expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan proposes changes, match the differing arguments to DSM and save a new plan.
3. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_share_permissions" "archive" {
  share = "archive"
  users = {}
  groups = {
    administrators = "read_write"
    team           = "read_only"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `groups` (Map of String) Complete explicit local-group policy, keyed by group name. Keep administrators = read_write to preserve management access.
- `share` (String) Shared-folder name and import identifier.
- `users` (Map of String) Complete explicit local-user policy, keyed by account name. Use an empty map for no individual overrides. Unlisted local users receive no explicit grant or deny.

### Read-Only

- `group_ids` (Map of Number) Observed numeric local-group identities used to reject replacement principals.
- `share_uuid` (String) Shared-folder identity used to reject a same-name replacement.
- `user_ids` (Map of Number) Observed numeric local-user identities used to reject replacement principals.
